# Droplet

Canonical: https://fuvji.github.io/droplet/
Source: https://github.com/fuvji/droplet
Version: 2.9.1
Platform: Windows 10/11 x64
Licence: proprietary, public source for inspection
Founder: @epufk

Droplet is a small, local keyboard-and-mouse macro suite for Minecraft Java,
branded Minecraft Zero Macro. It is a native Rust overlay with no runtime
dependencies, no network calls, no telemetry, and no game-memory access. It
injects ordinary keyboard and mouse input through Win32 SendInput and remains
visible to screen capture.

## Current release

- 2.9.1 portable executable: 592,384 bytes; signed MSIX: 301,774 bytes.
- Windows portable ZIP: https://fuvji.github.io/droplet/downloads/droplet-windows-x64.zip
- Windows MSIX: https://fuvji.github.io/droplet/downloads/droplet-windows-x64.msix
- Checksums: https://fuvji.github.io/droplet/downloads/SHA256SUMS.txt
- Release ledger: https://fuvji.github.io/droplet/releases.html
- Linux and macOS are not supported yet. The hook, window, and paint layers are
  Win32-specific; no .deb, AppImage, tar.gz, dmg, zip, or img is published.
- 19 release tests pass.
- Compact 624x408 graphite acrylic overlay with a 13 px shared corner radius.
- Borderless module cards with compact text ON/OFF pills. No module glyphs.
- Every trigger card switches between Hold (one-shot) and Toggle (latched repeat).
- Anchor defaults to a 37-43 ms window and still applies the 50 ms game tick floor; the card no longer prints a separate floor row.
- The tray icon was removed. A manual hide is sticky across focus changes.
  Ctrl + Right Shift shows or hides the panel.
- Dash, Shield, and Pearl select the slot and click in one SendInput batch.
- Pre-indexed trigger routing: 0.45 ns indexed versus 202.39 ns scanned (445x,
  routing only, not end-to-end latency).
- No streamproof or capture-concealment mode, no process hiding, no scan
  evasion, no anti-cheat bypass, no log erasure, and no zero-latency claim.
- No silent auto-updater. An update check would require a network path and a
  signed channel, which conflicts with the current no-network design.
- The site uses one local script for OS detection on the download page. It
  sends no data. There are no analytics, cookies, third-party scripts, external
  fonts, or ad clients.
